text: Ruvenna, May 14 — A failed cooling pump caused the outage at the Ruvenna data centre last spring, according to people familiar with the matter. The breakdown on April 22 triggered a rapid temperature rise in one server hall, forcing technicians to shut down power to 38 racks and interrupting service for several hours, the people said. Repairs and cleanup cost about 2.7 million dinars, while a review later found the pump’s bearing had worn past its service limit. The facility, run by Veylan Grid Services, has since added a redundant pump line and moved to hourly thermal checks, the people said. No customer data was lost, they added.
